To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

LIME explains the decision of any classifier by approximating locally with interpretable models, and provides the reasons why each input feature is important either to the overall prediction or to each explanation, and can approximate arbitrary residuals near inputs that are interpretable; and that LIME can pick inputs that spread the important value among inputs and makes predictions sensitive to inputs.

(1) explanations can be used to understand the predictions of any model; (2) explanations are more faithful and interpretable than black box models; (3) explanations are useful for making decisions in the presence of uncertainty; and (4) explanations can be generated in a computationally efficient and scalable way

(1) LIME is a novel method that explains the predictions made by any classifier in a locally faithful way, (2) LIME can be used to explain the output of complex models in a computationally efficient manner, and (3) LIME is competitive with existing state of the art methods in terms of predictive accuracy and explanation quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
turning machine learning interpretable.
turning black boxes into transparent instruments so that an individual can understand the decision made by a predictive model.

turning machine learning models and predictions that currently cannot be examined into accessible and interpretable predictions that facilitate trust and, as a result, the use of trained models in high-stakes decision-making domains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LIME is an extremely useful tool to help understand black-box models, especially when there is little to no access to their source code.
LIME is a novel and powerful explanation technique that can provide explanations for any model, and is not limited to a specific domain or a specific kind of models.
LIME is a very interesting work, which is well presented and which has a very good potential to be used in practice, but which is still far from being a finished product.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LIME helps to understand, to trust, to test and to debug machine learning models, and especially explain predictions to end users.
LIME is a simple, efficient, and flexible technique for visualizing and explaining the decision making process of a model.
we show how to trust neural networks (and models in general) in a post-hoc manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ultimate aim of explanation of a machine learning model should be to help the user understand not how, but why the model gave a given prediction.
the ultimate aim of faithfulness may not always be com- patible with explainability.
the ultimate aim of faithfulness should be to improve trust, and should not be restricted to interpretability under a fixed methodology.
